title: The order approved (1216)
hook: approved at last, Dominic's few friars scatter to the university towns

segments.voice: Yesterday, Prouille: before Dominic had a house of preaching brothers, he gathered a house of praying women. Your line was the nuns came first. Whose prayers did you give thanks for? Day one thousand two hundred thirty-two.

A small group of men in Toulouse. They have a name now, the pope's approval, and for the first time a future together. The sensible move is to stay. Build the house. Grow slowly, side by side, under the eye of the man who gathered them. Instead, the early accounts say, Dominic tells them to split up. Some to Paris. Some to Bologna. Some back to Spain. The brothers object. They are too few, too new, and they hardly know the work yet. He sends them anyway. Today: the order approved, and what it did first with its approval, which was scatter.
screen: `A NAME, AND THE POPE'S APPROVAL.` → `THE SENSIBLE MOVE: STAY.` → `DOMINIC SAYS: SPLIT UP.`

segments.voice: On paper the approval is quiet: the bishop of Rome signs, and a band of preachers from the south of France becomes an order of the whole Church. Their name says the job. The Order of Preachers. Not named for a place or a house, but for a task. And a task like that pulls you outward. Near its end, Mark's Gospel has Jesus sending his followers out. In the Douay-Rheims: "Go ye into the whole world, and preach the gospel to every creature." Dominic seems to have taken that at its word. A saying credited to him, in substance: grain heaped up in a barn goes bad; grain scattered on a field bears fruit. So the brothers went where the people were, and that meant the cities. Markets, workshops, crowds of strangers. And in some of those cities, something newer still: the universities, full of young men arguing about everything. The friars went straight into them. They studied there, preached there, and found new brothers there, as students and teachers asked for the habit. That choice shaped the whole order. The Rule of Saint Benedict asks a monk to promise stability, to stay with one community. A friar's life was built for the road. One detail stands out. The approval did not make Dominic careful. He had very few brothers, and he gave them away.
screen: `THE ORDER OF PREACHERS: NAMED FOR A TASK.` · `GRAIN HEAPED ROTS; GRAIN SCATTERED GROWS.` · `TO THE CITIES AND THE UNIVERSITIES.` · `HE HAD FEW BROTHERS, AND GAVE THEM AWAY.` · then, large: `GO YE INTO THE WHOLE WORLD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: pray for students. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one student you know. A kid doing homework at the kitchen table, a niece away at college, a coworker in night classes, maybe you. See them at the desk, the screen bright, the coffee gone cold. Breathe in, and hold them in mind. Breathe out any worry you carry for them. Then add someone you'll never meet: whoever is sitting alone in a library right now, stuck on the same page. If you pray, you can say a Hail Mary for both of them. If you don't, simply wish them a clear head and a good teacher. The bell holds the time.
The order approved. A small band became an order of the whole Church, and then scattered. This week ran from Francis on the bare ground to Dominic's friars on the road. Today's word.
Your line: to the cities. Today, take one good thing you'd usually keep to yourself, a book, an idea, a recipe, and send it out to someone. Day one thousand two hundred thirty-two.

howItsDone: Dominican friars live in communities, often in cities and near universities, and preach, teach and serve as chaplains; they write O.P., for the Order of Preachers, after their names.

original.note: Latin: the Order of Preachers, the Dominicans' official name. it's why friars write O.P. after their names.

trapdoor: what you thought: an order is a command, or a rule.
what it means: an order is a community with a shared life and a task. this one was approved for the whole Church, and named for preaching.
what a scholar hears: the friars were built for the road and the city, where the Rule of Benedict asks a monk to promise stability in one community.

notes: Claims rule: the year of approval (1216, Honorius III) and the year of the dispersal (1217) stay in the title only; the voice gives no dates or numbers of friars.
Confirm the dispersal to Paris, Bologna and Spain and the brothers' objection, as told in Jordan of Saxony's Libellus and later lives.
The grain saying is credited to Dominic in later tradition; it is given 'in substance' and not quoted. Confirm it is fair to call it 'a saying credited to him'.
Confirm that students and masters at Paris and Bologna entered the order (e.g., Reginald of Orléans, Jordan of Saxony), stated without names or numbers.
Week-end look-back (days 1226–1232) is kept to one line in the word segment.
Douay-Rheims wording of Mark 16:15 to confirm.
